definitions.explanation: Speaking or performing spontaneously without preparation or a script. Common in music, comedy, and acting.

examples.japanese: このシーンはアドリブで{演|えん}じた。
ジャズはアドリブが{重要|じゅうよう}だ。
{彼|かれ}はアドリブが{得意|とくい}だ。

notes:
アドリブ refers to spontaneous, unscripted performance or speech. Borrowed from Latin "ad libitum" (at pleasure), via English.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- アドリブで{演|えん}じる: to perform ad-lib
- アドリブが{利|き}く: to be good at improvising
- アドリブを{入|い}れる: to throw in an ad-lib
- アドリブ{演奏|えんそう}: improvised performance

USAGE:
Most commonly heard in entertainment contexts: jazz improvisation, comedy ({漫才|まんざい}, variety shows), theater, and film. Also used more broadly for any unscripted speaking, such as presentations or interviews. As a な-adjective: アドリブな{対応|たいおう} (an improvised response).

CONTRAST:
- {即興|そっきょう}: improvisation (more formal/literary, used in music and art)
- {台本|だいほん}なし: without a script (descriptive phrase)
